cases.prompt: A colleague's count record for a synthetic suspension reads: 20 µL cells + 30 µL trypan blue; chamber A 22 cells, chamber B 61 cells (one large square each); blue cells on the right edge counted as dead; 'viability 96%, culture healthy, seed tomorrow'. Write a review of this record: what you would check or redo before trusting the count, how you would calculate and report concentration, viability and counting uncertainty, and what the viability figure can and cannot support.

rubric.criterion: Uses the dilution factor (20 + 30)/20 = 2.5 and the chamber's stated volume per large square, and asks whether the suspension was mixed before sampling
Recognises that 22 and 61 differ by far more than √(22 + 61) ≈ 9.1, so the chambers should be reloaded rather than averaged
Corrects the boundary error: cells touching the right edge are excluded before any stain decision, so the stained tally and viability must be recounted
Reports viable concentration, viability and the Poisson uncertainty with the N it was computed from, and notes the systematic errors that uncertainty excludes
States that trypan-blue exclusion shows membrane integrity at counting time and cannot establish health, growth, phenotype or freedom from contamination

limitations: A zero-point self-check on a synthetic record; it is not a grade or a competency record, and your laboratory's procedures govern real counts.
